tasks.title: Problem 1
tasks.statement: This is the sky above Keszthely at midnight. The projected sky does not show any Solar System objects.

parts.question: There are 3 novae on the projected sky at 2nd magnitude. Mark their positions by circles on the star chart. (Please circle only 3 stars. If there are more than 3 circles, then each one in a wrong location will result in 1 point deduction.)
parts.reference: Solution: See the stellar map. Marking: 3 points/each nova (wrong position: minus 1 point) maximum: 9 points

parts.question: The Messier objects have been removed from the star chart given you. Mark all the Messier list globular clusters present in the projected sky on the star chart using crosses (X) and write the Messier number of each object near the cross marks.
parts.reference: Solution: Visible globular clusters: M2, M13, M15, M30, M56, M71, M72, M92. Marking: good position (signed by X): max. 3 points/each. X inside the inner circle = 2 points, outer circle 1 point. Good Messier number 1 point/each. maximum: 24 points

parts.question: The projected sky corresponds to the second half of which month (at midnight CEST) in Keszthely? Circle the correct month. JAN / FEB / MAR / APR / MAY / JUN / JUL / AUG / SEP / OCT / NOV / DEC
parts.reference: Solution: October 19, 2019. Marking: October = 2 points, September or November = 1 point maximum: 2 points

parts.question: What is the local sidereal time? (To an accuracy of 15 minutes.)
parts.reference: Solution: sidereal time is 1h 00m. Gamma Cassiopeiae is near upper culmination (RA 00h 57m). Marking: 1h 00m = 3 points, +15m (1h 15m or 0h 45m) = 2 points, +30m (1h 30m or 0h 30m) = 1 point maximum: 3 points

parts.question: List six zodiacal constellations, which are partly or entirely visible. (Use the official IAU abbreviations or IAU designation. Every constellation named which is not visible in the projected sky will result in 1 point deduction.)
parts.reference: Solution: Sagittarius (Sgr), Capricornus (Cap), Aquarius (Aqr), Pisces (Psc), Aries (Ari), Taurus (Tau), Gemini (Gem), Cancer (Cnc). Marking: 1 points/each constellation maximum: 6 points

tasks.title: Problem 2
tasks.statement: We are standing somewhere on the Earth. The projected sky does not show any Solar System objects.

parts.question: Determine the geographical latitude of this observing site: …………….° In which hemisphere is the site situated? N / S (Circle the right one.)
parts.reference: Solution: Geographical latitude of this observing site: 25°. Constellation Crux shows us the direction the southern celestial pole. Marking: latitude between 24–26° = 2 points, within +3° (22°, 23°, 27°, 28°) = 1 point. Southern hemisphere = 1 point. maximum: 3 points

parts.question: Determine the azimuth of the 3 brightest stars on the projected sky. Azimuth is measured from North towards the East. Write the name of these stars in English or using their Bayer designation and their azimuths in the list below.
parts.reference: Solution: 1st Sirius (α CMa) Az: 82°, 2nd Canopus (α Car) Az: 42°, 3rd Toliman (α Cen) Az: 331°. Marking: Proper name on a dotted line = 2 points each. Azimuth angles within +2° = 2 points each, within +5° 1 point each. Incorrect position in a list = -1 point. maximum: 12 points

parts.question: Yellow × signs show the position of 3 comets. Which comet is closest to the ecliptic? (Circle the number below.) 1 / 2 / 3
parts.reference: Solution: The number two comet is in closest position to ecliptic. Marking: Number two comet = 2 points maximum: 2 points

parts.question: List nine constellations that contain circumpolar stars seen from the given observing site. (Use the official IAU abbreviations or IAU designation.)
parts.reference: Solution and Marking: 1 point for each of: Octans (Oct), Mensa (Men), Chamaeleon (Cha), Apus (Aps), Hydrus (Hyi), Volans (Vol), Carina (Car), Musca (Mus), Circinus (Cir), Triangulum Australe (TrA), Pavo (Pav), Indus (Ind), Tucana (Tuc), Horologium (Hor), Ara (Ara). maximum: 9 points

parts.question: Mintaka (δ Orionis) is setting at this moment. How many hours earlier did it rise? (To an accuracy of 15 minutes.)
parts.reference: Solution: 12h. delta Orionis is approximately located on celestial equator. Marking: 2 points for exact value. maximum: 2 points

tasks.title: Problem 3
tasks.statement: For this view, we are now standing on the Moon. At this instant viewed, the Earth is centrally eclipsing the Sun (see the red circle on the sky). Consequently the Moon is at one of its nodes now. Assume the longitudinal and latitudinal librations are exactly 0° at this moment.

parts.question: At the time of this observation, which season is it in Hungary? (Circle the correct answer.) Spring / Summer / Autumn / Winter
parts.reference: Solution: Autumn (fall). Marking: right answer (Autumn) is 2 points. maximum: 2 points

parts.question: There is a yellow circle on the projected sky (next to the red circle), which denotes minor planet Juno, which is at a distance of exactly 3 au from the Sun at this moment. Estimate its distance to the Moon at this instant. (Rounded to the nearest integer in units of million km.) Assume all orbits to be circular.
parts.reference: Solution: 598.8 (~599) million km. Marking: 2 points for +1 million km, 1 point for +2 million km. maximum: 2 points

parts.question: Approximately how much time (in Earth days) after the projected event will the Sun set at your observing site? …the Earth set at your observing site?
parts.reference: Solution 1: Sunset can be observed about 3-4 days later (3.28 days = 78.7 hours). Marking: between 3-4 days: 4 points, 2 or 5 days: 2 point. Solution 2: Earth set can be observed: never. Marking: the good answer is 2 points. maximum: 4 + 2 = 6 points

parts.question: Determine the Lunar (Selenographic) coordinates of this observing site and the name of the large surface lunar area where your observing site is situated using the official IAU nomenclature.
parts.reference: Solution 1: latitude: 0° , longitude: 50° E. Marking for latitude: within +2° 3 points, +5° 2 points; for longitude: within +2° 3 points, +5° 2 points (max 6 points). Solution 2: Mare Fecunditatis. Marking: any one of the accepted names: 6 points. maximum: 12 points

parts.question: Estimate the distance from the observing site to the Apollo-11 landing site (0.6875 N, 23.4333 E):
parts.reference: Solution: about 800 km. Marking: +100 km (700-900 km) 6 points, +200 km (600-699 or 901-1000) 5 points, +300 km (500-599 or 1001-1100) 4 points, +400 km (400-499 or 1101-1200) 3 points. maximum: 6 points
